key_insight: PRISM-CAFO introduces a prior-conditioned, infrastructure-first pipeline that segments and maps CAFO infrastructure (e.g., barns, lagoons, pens) from aerial and satellite imagery, yielding scalable, explainable detections for large-area monitoring. By conditioning segmentation on infrastructure priors, the approach improves interpretability and robustness compared with object-first detection alone.
problem_solved: Accurate, scalable, and interpretable mapping of Concentrated Animal Feeding Operations (CAFOs) from remote-sensing imagery—a critical need for tracking environmental and public-health risks as CAFOs grow in number and spatial extent.
method: Prior-conditioned segmentation: focus the model on infrastructure classes (barns, lagoons, feedlots) using domain priors to guide learning and reduce false positives.
Multi-resolution remote-sensing fusion: combine aerial and satellite imagery to scale detection across local and regional extents while preserving fine structural detail.
Explainable mapping pipeline: produce human-interpretable outputs (segmentation masks, infrastructure attributes, uncertainty maps) enabling downstream verification and policymaking.
impact: Provides a practical blueprint for building scalable, interpretable geospatial ML systems for environmental monitoring; useful for practitioners working on remote sensing, domain priors, model explainability, and public-good mapping applications.
visual_elements: Pipeline flowchart: prior conditioning → segmentation → attribute extraction → geospatial map overlay (clear, stepwise blocks).
Before/after zoomed imagery: raw aerial/satellite tile vs. segmented infrastructure masks (barns, lagoons, pens) to show improvement.
Geographic map with CAFO detections and uncertainty heatmap to convey scale and confidence across regions.
Legend/infographic card showing key metrics: infrastructure classes, example attributes (area, proximity to waterways), and explainability cues.
paper_title: PRISM-CAFO: Prior-conditioned Remote-sensing Infrastructure Segmentation and Mapping for CAFOs
paper_authors: Oishee Bintey Hoque, Nibir Chandra Mandal, Kyle Luong, Amanda Wilson, Samarth Swarup
